title: February-March warmth gave no clear common link to paired butterfly sighting gaps in Japan in 1953-2020
abstract: We tested whether February-March warmth changed the first-sighting date of Papilio machaon relative to Pieris rapae. Four separate region and period models used 2,945 paired station-years at 58 Japan stations in 1953-2020. Models controlled station and report-location pairs, year, and January temperature. Slopes were -1.99, +2.57, +0.72 and +0.85 days per C. All four intervals included zero after correction for four tests. Southern slopes were +2.50 and +2.79 with a linear year trend, with corrected intervals above zero. Year effects reduced those estimates and precision. Thus, a clear common local response did not repeat. This does not show equal biological responses. Unknown search effort and abundance, missing dates, changing report locations, small local weather contrasts, and coarse temperature data limit inference. Monthly weather windows extend past some sightings. The study does not test pollution, daily extremes, harmful mismatch, or causal climate-change effects. The package preserves source hashes, the paired panel, code, all planned models, figures, an independent regression check and reproduction instructions.

display.caption: Local February-March temperature slopes for Papilio minus Pieris first-sighting dates. Thick bars show marginal 95% intervals. Thin bars show 98.75% intervals for four tests. All four corrected intervals include zero.

Planned model and sample checks. Bars show marginal 95% intervals. Southern positive slopes with linear year trends became smaller and less precise with year effects. This is model dependence, not a causal comparison. The late northern linear-trend point has no bar because its two-way variance was nonpositive.
